.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes made to the forecast. Expecting very warm
temperatures, dry and breezy conditions behind frontal passage 
on Friday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Very warm to end the work week, then seasonal conditions 
  for Halloween Weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Very warm to end the work week, then seasonal 
conditions for Halloween Weekend.

A weak, dry cold front is progged to cross the region Friday 
morning, possibly bringing some drizzle to the higher elevations of 
the Alleghenies. High pressure builds into the region Friday 
afternoon through the weekend. Expect well above normal temperatures 
Friday as highs reach the mid to upper 70s. Would not be surprised 
if a spot or two in central VA reached 80F briefly. Some passing 
clouds are likely Friday morning to early afternoon, though the 
background environment is forecast to be very dry, so not expecting 
much impact on temperatures. Downsloping winds make for a breezy 
afternoon as winds gust around 20-25 mph, especially along/north of 
I-66/US-50. 

Eventually, some cooler temperatures moves in Friday night through 
the weekend. Expect seasonable and dry conditions as high pressure 
holds firm. A shortwave trough passing just south of the area on 
Sunday won't amount to much as it lacks sufficient moisture or 
forcing to produce widespread shower activity.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Rain chances remain uncertain for the first half of 
next week with a more appreciable chance during the latter half of 
next week.

High pressure should hold strong enough Sunday into Monday, where 
rain chances could be squashed or be confined to upslope rain 
showers or sprinkles in the higher western elevations. As for 
temperatures each day, they should be seasonable with highs in the 
lower to middle 60s.

By Tuesday into Wednesday, a strong trough of low pressure will 
begin to push eastward from the Great Plains toward the Mississippi 
and Ohio Valleys. This will aid in weakening the high pressure over 
us. There are increasingly better rain chances ahead during this 
period. We may be waiting until Wednesday night and Thursday to see 
some of these rain showers, but the chances are on the rise. 
Temperatures will become warmer as well Tuesday and Wednesday and 
reaching into the lower to middle 70s ahead of a strong trough from 
the west.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR conditions are forecast to persist through the weekend as high 
pressure builds into the region. Breezy west to northwest winds 
could gust up to 20-25 knots Friday afternoon in wake of a dry cold 
front passage Friday morning.

VFR conditions Sunday through Monday night. Light southeast to 
southerly winds around 5 knots each period.

&&

.MARINE...
A dry cold front is forecast to move across the waters Friday 
morning, then high pressure builds across the region through the 
weekend. SCA conditions are expected Friday afternoon into Friday 
night, especially over the open waters of the bay where northerly 
channeling effects are maximized. Winds diminish Saturday morning, 
then drop below SCA levels by early Saturday afternoon.

No marine hazards expected Sunday through Monday night. Winds 
light southeast to southerly winds 5 to 10 knots through the 
period.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tidal anomalies have remained steady today, so it is possible 
sensitive locations approach minor flood stage during evening's high 
tide cycle. After that, offshore flow develops behind a cold frontal 
passage Friday morning. Winds turn back around out of the south at 
low speeds which could cause a modest rebound in tides by Sunday 
afternoon.
